summary: Every pair can change the final winner, so all n nodes must be inspected; the one-pass reference meets that linear lower bound with constant auxiliary storage.

optimality.argument: If an algorithm skips any pair, that pair's legal even and odd values can be chosen to award the decisive point to either team without changing the inspected nodes. A correct algorithm must therefore examine all n/2 pairs, while the reference performs constant work per pair.

replacement_checks.evidence: An uninspected pair can reverse a tied score or change which team wins by one point, so its values cannot be ignored.
The reference advances by exactly two nodes per iteration and uses only a score difference and one traversal pointer.
Authored cases cover the minimum list, unanimous wins for each team, tied scores, alternating winners, boundary values, and a result decided by the final pair.
